title: Creamy Cashew and Yoghurt Chicken Curry with Cardamom
summary: Chicken thighs marinated in yoghurt and ginger are simmered in a smooth cashew and caramelised onion sauce warmed through with whole spices, finished with cream and toasted cashews.
equipment: large heavy pot or casserole with a lid

ingredients.item: boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into 4 cm pieces
fine sea salt or table salt
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Marinate the chicken
steps.text: Mix the chicken with the yoghurt, ginger, garlic and salt in the large bowl. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 8 hours. The yoghurt's gentle acidity works into the meat over time, helping to tenderise it and carry the ginger and garlic flavour right through.

steps.title: Soften the cashews
steps.text: Pulse the cashews in the blender to coarse crumbs, then add the hot water, blend briefly and leave for 15 minutes to soften. Softening the nuts first means they'll blend to a completely smooth, grit-free cream rather than staying gritty in the finished sauce.

steps.title: Caramelise the onions
steps.text: Heat the 3 tbsp ghee in the pot over medium heat, add the onions and salt and cook for 10-15 minutes, stirring often, until deep golden brown, turning the heat down if they start to catch. Tip the onions and tomato into the blender with the softened cashews and blend until completely smooth, about 2 minutes. Cooking the onions this far brings out a deep natural sweetness that underpins the whole sauce.

steps.title: Bloom the spices
steps.text: Add the 1 tbsp ghee to the empty pot over medium heat and fry the cardamom, cloves, cinnamon and bay leaf for 30-60 seconds until fragrant. Stir in the ground coriander, turmeric, chilli and pepper for 30 seconds, then add the cashew-onion sauce and the 120 ml water, scraping the base. Bring to a simmer, cover and cook gently for 10 minutes; frying the spices briefly in hot fat releases far more of their aroma than simply simmering them in liquid.

steps.title: Cook the chicken gently
steps.text: Stir in the chicken with all its marinade, return to a gentle simmer, cover and cook for 15-20 minutes, stirring now and then, until the chicken reaches 74°C in the thickest piece. Keep the heat low enough that the sauce only just bubbles, since a hard boil can cause the yoghurt to split instead of staying silky.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Meanwhile, toast the 20 g cashews in the dry frying pan for 3-4 minutes until golden. Remove the whole spices from the curry, stir in the cream and heat for 1 minute, then scatter over the toasted cashews and coriander. Serve with rice or flatbread.

tips: Keep the curry at a gentle simmer once the yoghurt and cream go in — boiling hard can make the sauce split rather than staying smooth and creamy.
Remember to fish out the cardamom pods, cloves, cinnamon stick and bay leaf before serving, as biting into a whole spice is an unpleasant surprise.
Letting the onions go properly deep golden brown, not just soft, is what gives the sauce its rounded sweetness, so don't rush this step.
Soaking the cashews in hot water before blending is what makes the sauce silky rather than gritty, so don't skip the 15-minute rest.
Marinating the chicken for the full 8 hours, if you have time, gives a noticeably more tender result than the minimum 30 minutes.
storage: Cool quickly and refrigerate within 1 hour; use within 3 days and reheat only once until piping hot (74°C). This curry also freezes well for up to 3 months. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
